summary:
BioOrbit is an astronaut health-monitoring application designed to support astronauts’ physical and cognitive well-being during space missions. We developed a health dashboard that displays important health indicators, including heart rate, blood oxygen (SpO₂), blood pressure, body temperature, sleep, and activity, alongside personal baseline readings to help monitor changes over time.

To make the platform more comprehensive, we added cognitive thinking games to encourage astronauts to exercise their memory, attention, and problem-solving skills. We also developed a Departments page, where users can view health information for other astronauts and support a broader understanding of crew well-being. In addition, our research search engine allows astronauts to search through a collected library of space-health research and find relevant information on topics they want to understand.
BioOrbit addresses the challenge by bringing health monitoring, cognitive engagement, crew information, and research access together in one platform. This is important because astronauts face unique physical and mental demands in space. By making relevant information easier to access and helping monitor individual and crew health, BioOrbit aims to support awareness, informed decisions, and overall astronaut well-being throughout a mission.
details: BioOrbit is an astronaut health and well-being application designed to support astronauts during space missions, especially long-duration missions where monitoring physical health, maintaining cognitive abilities, and accessing important information are essential. The app includes a health dashboard that displays sleep, heart rate, blood oxygen (SpO₂), blood pressure, body temperature, and physical activity, comparing readings with personal historical averages. It also features cognitive thinking games designed to exercise memory, attention, and problem-solving, a Departments page where astronauts can view other crew members' health information, and a research search engine that helps users find relevant information from research collected by our team. Our intended impact is to make health information more organized and accessible, encourage awareness of personal health patterns, support cognitive engagement, and contribute to astronauts' well-being during space exploration. We hope to develop the project further by integrating real wearable data, expanding the cognitive activities, and improving access to crew health information and scientific research. We created the prototype using MIT App Inventor, including its Designer tools to build the screens, buttons, labels, and layouts, and its visual block-based programming system to create the dashboard, calculate averages, navigate between screens, and search research entries. We did not use a separate text-based coding language or dedicated hardware to build the prototype; the wearable connection is currently an interface for future integration, not a working smartwatch connection. The creative aspect of BioOrbit is that it combines physical health indicators, cognitive activities, crew information, and research access in one application rather than treating them as separate features. During development, our team considered astronauts' physical and cognitive well-being, the challenges of long-duration space missions, ease of use, accessibility of information, personal health differences, and the importance of presenting health data responsibly. We used sample demonstration readings and sample history values to test the dashboard and baseline calculations, not real astronaut medical records. Our research library contains information collected by our team. We have not documented a specific NASA dataset, NASA API, or external partner dataset as being integrated into the current prototype, and we do not claim that the app currently receives live NASA or wearable data. Overall, BioOrbit aims to be a useful foundation for a more connected, accessible, and astronaut-focused health support platform.
